summary.text: A 55-year-old male construction worker with a long history of smoking and alcohol consumption presented with sudden-onset vertigo, imbalance, headache and diplopia; examination showed anisocoria with right-sided miosis and ptosis, left-sided upper and lower limb hypesthesia and gait instability.
Laboratory tests including inflammatory markers and coagulation parameters were unremarkable and non-contrast head CT showed no acute ischemia or hemorrhage.

MRI showed a 9-mm diffusion-restricted focus in the right posterolateral medulla consistent with acute ischemia, and angio-MRI showed signs of proximal intracranial right vertebral artery dissection with approximately 50% luminal reduction; the case is reported as Wallenberg syndrome secondary to vertebral artery dissection.
Electrocardiogram, echocardiogram and 24-hour Holter monitoring revealed no arrhythmias.

Antiplatelet monotherapy was initiated and the patient was referred for follow-up at the Internal Medicine department; the abstract also reports early rehabilitation and vascular risk factor management. No outcome is reported.

summary.text: A 41-year-old man without a previous remarkable medical history, particularly head/neck trauma, presented to the emergency department with headache, vertigo, dysphonia, dysphagia, loss of balance with gait instability, impaired taste sensation and loss of pain and temperature sensation on the right face and contralateral body over five hours, with preserved muscle strength.
Examination showed right-sided ptosis, horizontal nystagmus, impaired temperature and pain sensation on the right face and contralateral body, and leftward uvular deviation.
Laboratory testing revealed activated protein C resistance and Factor V Leiden mutation; other Table 1 thrombophilia and autoimmune results are recorded individually.

Head CT was inconclusive; MRI showed an infra-centimetric acute ischemic lesion in the right posterolateral medulla consistent with Wallenberg syndrome, without evidence of vertebral artery dissection. Atrial fibrillation was ruled out by ECG, echocardiogram and Holter monitoring.
Treatment included blood pressure optimization, antiplatelet therapy, statin for secondary prevention, deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis and early rehabilitation. No outcome is reported.
